maria: Heads up — started seeing a cluster of OOMs on prod vocoder at 10:12 UTC after the allocator change (expandable_segments toggled). stack traces look like transient alloc spikes during long-context samples. anyone free to triage? :wave:
aj: saw alerts. quick glance at profiler shows high external fragmentation in cuda reserved pool — a lot of tiny frees + re-allocs around KV cache churn. p95 allocation size small but many of them.
chen: can you paste the `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` and the small profile snippet? also what model/seq_len were affected?
maria: seq_len ~ 8192 on a few long sampling jobs. env: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:16,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6,expandable_segments:1`
maria: attach: ``
# torch.cuda.memory_summary() snippet (staging repro)
| allocated bytes | 18.2GB |
| reserved bytes  | 24.0GB |
| active segments | 312    |
| free segments   | 48     |
``
aj: that reserved/active ratio + high segment count is the fragmentation smell. small max_split_size_mb -> allocator splits large blocks into many small ones which then don't coalesce when expandable_segments=1 leads to lots of variable-sized segments.
aj: quick mitigation to try on canary: bump `max_split_size_mb` to 64 or 128, and raise `garbage_collection_threshold` to 0.85 so the allocator releases cached blocks earlier. also try `expandable_segments=0` to keep segment size bounded.
chen: agree. additionally the KV cache pattern: we allocate many small buffers per token and per head during reorders. Buffer reuse (prealloc per-request workspace) would avoid churn. quick snippet: 
```
# preallocate workspace once per worker
_ws = torch.empty((max_kv_bytes,), dtype=torch.uint8, device='cuda')
# slice for per-request views rather than new allocations
```

maria: ran a staging canary with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64,garbage_collection_threshold:0.85,expandable_segments:0` — no OOMs during the 30m stress run. p95 latency went +5ms, throughput -1%.
chen: tradeoff looks fine. we should also add a short-lived GC call after heavy batch windows in the runtime path: `torch.cuda.memory.empty_cache()` is cheap and helps reclaim cached segments for other tasks. schedule it only when fragmentation metric crosses threshold.
aj: logging/action items: (1) deploy canary change to 10% traffic, (2) add allocator metrics: reserved/allocated ratio, segment_count, avg_segment_size, fragmentation_score, (3) instrument KV cache to report avg allocation size and reuse hit-rate, (4) add a small E2E stress test for long-context samples to catch regressions.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-178065 — OOM spike during vocoder long-context sampling. Pager rules unchanged.
maria: will roll the canary in 15m and post results. thanks all. :thumbsup:
